title: Rainbow Ramsey for computably omega-bounded barriers admits strong cone avoidance
source_title: Ramsey-like theorems for the Schreier barrier

standard_prerequisites.name: Barriers, rainbow colourings, progressive colourings and the cone-avoidance theorem
standard_prerequisites.statement: A barrier is a family of finite sets of natural numbers that is closed under taking initial segments and meets every infinite set exactly once along its increasing enumeration; a set is a rainbow for a colouring of a barrier when the sets it induces by initial segments take pairwise distinct colours, and the article's principle for barriers asks for such a rainbow. The same section proves that bounded progressive colourings of the barrier admit strong cone avoidance, and it proves separately that every colouring of a barrier can be turned computably into a constrained progressive colouring all of whose infinite free sets are rainbows for the original colouring. The author's own notions and those two results are the allowed inputs.
standard_prerequisites.use: The counted corollary transfers strong cone avoidance from progressive colourings to rainbow colourings on computably bounded barriers, and it is quoted as the barrier-level form of the article's main avoidance theorem.

core_obligations: Fix the cone: given a set Z and a set D not computable from Z, and an instance of the barrier principle given by a bound h and a colouring of a computably bounded barrier into finitely many colours, one must produce an infinite rainbow free of the cone of D over Z (source lines 1295-1297).

Reduce the rainbow instance to a progressive instance: normalise the bound so that it dominates the number of colours, apply the article's reduction which turns the colouring of the barrier computably into a constrained progressive colouring on that barrier while keeping every infinite free set a rainbow, and note that it is also bounded by the normalised bound (source line 1297).
Extend the resulting colouring to all finite sets by giving the empty value outside the barrier, which keeps it constrained and progressive (source line 1299).

Apply the strong cone-avoidance theorem to the extended colouring to obtain an infinite free set avoiding the cone of D over Z, and observe that the same set is an infinite rainbow for the original colouring, which is the corollary (source line 1301).

proof_roadmap.step: Fix the cone and an instance of the barrier principle, and recall the reduction to a constrained progressive colouring.
Extend the colouring outside the barrier by the empty value.
Apply cone avoidance and read the resulting free set as a rainbow.

difficulty_reason: 计数单元是 arXiv:2412.11598v3 的**无 label** Corollary（源 1290-1293 行，证明 1294-1302 行）：对每个可计算 ω-有界 barrier B 与 k∈N⁺，RRT^B_k 具有强锥回避。关键操作不是例行核验：证明要先把任意 RRT 实例（k 色、barrier B、界 h）**归约**成 §6 里那条「f′ 可计算、k-constrained progressive、且其无穷 free 集恰是 rainbow」的命题（1297 行，并需把 h 正规化成 ≥k），再把障碍外的输出补成 ∅ 以把着色扩展到全部有限集、保持 constrained 与 progressive（1299 行），最后对该扩展着色套用强锥回避定理得到 D ⩽̸_T G⊕Z 的无穷 free 集 G，并由归约性质读出 G 同时是原着色的无穷 rainbow（1301 行）。难点在于把两条不同层次的结论（rainbow 归约 + progressive 锥回避）串联，并处理「barrier 外取值」这一技术细节；原文位置在证明的 1295-1297、1299、1301 行。
